attempts.summary:
Implemented persistent traffic mirroring on node1 (Debian/SONiC-VS) using iptables mangle TEE targets: all traffic to/from node2 (10.100.28.11) is cloned in PREROUTING (incoming from node2) and OUTPUT (outgoing to node2) with gateway 10.100.28.12 (node3), preserving original src/dst addressing so node3's tcpdump sees packets "addressed elsewhere" while the original node1<->node2 path is untouched (0% packet loss throughout all tests). Config was made boot-persistent via a systemd oneshot unit (traffic-mirror.service, enabled) plus /etc/modules-load.d for xt_TEE. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured healthy baselines (boot_id, mirroring state, working ping) on all three nodes, restarted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time via `systemctl reboot`, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and re-verified mirroring functionality end-to-end after each restart and once more after all three had cycled.

Note: an initial attempt using tc/mirred + gretap (ERSPAN-style) encapsulation was tried first but the mirrored frames never actually left node1's eth0 (kernel accepted them into the gretap device but they didn't reach node3), even though a manually-addressed GRE tunnel between the same endpoints worked fine — this was abandoned in favor of the iptables TEE approach, which worked immediately and is simpler/more standard for this passive-mirroring use case.
